en tallerken lungemos med tre poteter i
a plate of lung mash with three potatoes in it

36064.etyen:
From lunge (“lung”) + mos (“mash, purée”), literally “lung mash”.
The first element lunge (“lung”) is inherited from lunga (“lung”), from *lungô (“lung”), ultimately from *h₁lengʷʰ- (“light, agile, nimble”), probably referring to the lungs as comparatively light organs. The second element mos (“mash, purée”) was borrowed from mos (“mush, porridge”), from *mōsą (“food, mush”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk lungemos, Danish lungemos and Swedish lungmos.

1001952.etyen:
From Berthel (“male given name”) + -sen (“patronymic suffix meaning “son of””), originally a patronymic meaning “son of Berthel”. The given name Berthel is a spelling variant of Bertel, a Danish form of German Berthold, traditionally interpreted as a Germanic compound meaning “bright ruler” or “bright power”.
Compare Danish Berthelsen (“patronymic surname”).
